# FAQ-030 Engineering FAQ #30

Revision: Rev A

Q: What is the required maintenance interval for shot media top-up on Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01), and why is that interval used?
A: The shot media top-up interval for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) is 40 hours. Background: consistent media size and quantity are required to maintain blast energy and part finish. Rationale: a fixed operating-hour interval prevents gradual depletion and segregation that lead to inconsistent surface condition. Example: if production runs are heavy, schedule a top-up at the next planned service opportunity that coincides with end of a shift to avoid mid-run interruptions. Records to keep: log the equipment id, date and time of top-up, operator name, batch of media used, and any observed contamination or abnormal media wear. Reference procedures: see SOP-P3-L2-04 for blast cabinet handling and media classification.

Q: What is the specified main ram bolt torque for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03), and how should it be applied?
A: The main ram bolt torque for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03) is 1575 N·m. Background: correct bolt preload secures the ram assembly and maintains alignment under load. Rationale: using the specified torque prevents bolt yielding and ensures clamping force within design limits. Application steps: clean threads, apply the manufacturer-specified lubricant to threads if required by the applicable maintenance specification in SOP-P2-L4-02, and use a calibrated torque wrench rated for the required range. Perform torque in the pattern specified by the press assembly drawing to achieve uniform preload. Records to keep: maintenance record with equipment id, bolt identification if available, torque value applied, tool calibration id, technician initials, and any deviation or re-torque actions.

Q: Which lubricant part number is approved for Hot Forge CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P1-L1-CN02), and what are the usage instructions?
A: The lubricant part number for Hot Forge CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P1-L1-CN02) is CFW-LUB-508. Background: using the correct lubricant ensures spindle and axis drive longevity and consistent thermal behavior during machining. Rationale: approved lubricants are qualified for viscosity, additive chemistry, and compatibility with seals and materials in the machine. Usage instructions: apply per the machine manufacturer recommendations and the lubrication schedule documented in SOP-P1-L1-05. Store lubricant in labeled containers, control stock rotation, and do not dilute or mix with other lubricants. Records to keep: batch or lot id from the lubricant container, date of application, quantity used, machine id, and responsible technician.

Q: What is the system pressure limit for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03), and what safeguards should be in place?
A: The system pressure limit for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03) is 295 bar. Background: the hydraulic system components, hoses, valves, and actuators are rated to a maximum service pressure; exceeding that rating risks component failure and safety hazards. Rationale: setting relief valves and pressure monitoring alarms at or below the limit provides protection against transient overpressure events. Safeguards: verify relief valve settings and alarm thresholds during start-up checks, inspect pressure lines for wear, and ensure pressure gauges are calibrated and readable. Records to keep: calibration certificates for pressure gauges, relief valve set records, start-up check logs including instrument readings, and any incident reports related to overpressure. See SOP-P3-L2-04 for hydraulic system maintenance practices.

Q: What is the maximum quench delay allowed for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02), and how is compliance demonstrated?
A: The quench delay maximum for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02) is 20 seconds. Background: quench delay influences microstructure and mechanical properties; control of delay is critical to meet heat-treat specifications. Rationale: limiting delay prevents undesirable transformation and ensures repeatable part performance. Compliance demonstration: time each load transfer from furnace to quench and record the measured delay. If automated transfer is used, validate the automation cycle time and log the event timestamps. Records to keep: heat-treat job record with furnace id, lot id, operator, start and quench timestamps, measured delay, and any deviations or corrective actions. Reference procedures: follow SOP-P2-L4-02 for heat-treat cycle control and SOP-P3-L4-04 for furnace safety and verification where applicable.

Related documents: SOP-P1-L1-05, SOP-P2-L4-02, SOP-P3-L2-04

Document control note: maintain the records specified above in the document control system under the equipment file for each referenced asset.
